lines.en: [You have died.]
The aftermath of this death was severe.
It seemed to be the shock of having Stories torn from me by the [Eater of Dreams].
The [Fourth Wall]'s restorative ability had helped me recover quickly, but it is difficult to make something as whole as it was before simply by piecing it back together after it has broken.
‘Ugh, my head······.’
I spent three days only half in my right mind.
My consciousness repeatedly faded and returned. Each time I regained awareness in my soul state, I reflected on everything that had happened, one thing at a time.
‘Once we're through this scenario, the story will get back on track.’

Over the course of nine scenarios, I had substantially disrupted the original story's course. From small changes, like saving a few characters, to large ones, like changing how the scenarios unfolded.

Of course, changing the scenarios didn't make the elements of the original story useless. Yoo Joonghyuk had lived well over a hundred rounds, and even with the scenarios changed, there was still more information than I could possibly use.
Even so, to take advantage of the overarching course of events, some parts definitely needed to follow the original scenarios.
Fortunately, the [Seoul Dome Scenario] was a closed scenario.

There had been a battle between countries along the way, and a few incidents that gave me reason to worry about the butterfly effect, but the overarching course of the <Star Stream> was still just as I remembered it.
Moreover, the characters had grown far more than I had expected, so we had already secured enough strength to take the lead in what came next.
I observed the characters one by one through the ‘Third-Person Viewpoint.’
The first person I checked on was Jung Heewon, the ‘Judge of Evil.’
“It's still hard to control. My sponsor says that once I can use this perfectly, I'll be able to fight that tentacle monster too······ But I have no idea when I'll get there.”
Jung Heewon muttered as she withdrew the white flames.
She had barely featured in the original story, but she had become the strongest fighter among the characters I had recruited.

She had awakened ‘Judge of Evil,’ one of the best attributes in Ways of Survival, and had even inherited Uriel's [Hell Flames Ignition]. Given enough time at this rate, she might rank not only among the hundred strongest people in Ways of Survival, but even among the top ten.
Lee Hyunsung, who had been facing Jung Heewon in their sparring match, spoke.
“Still, you're improving little by little, Heewon-ssi.”
“You seem to have improved a lot too, Hyunsung-ssi. You're getting quite good at covering your whole body in steel now.”
She had probably said it without knowing any of this, but Jung Heewon's reassurance wasn't wrong.

There weren't many rounds in which Lee Hyunsung began inheriting [Steel Transformation] before the [Seoul Dome] scenario ended. But perhaps he wasn't satisfied with his achievements; he looked completely unsure of himself.
“I'm trying, but······ I still have a long way to go before I can be of help to Dokja-ssi.”
Some people do better when someone stays beside them, constantly saying, ‘You're doing well, you're doing well.’
Lee Hyunsung was exactly that sort of person.
[A constellation who does not yet have a name has sponsored incarnation Lee Hyunsung with 100 coins.]
“D-Dokja-ssi?”
A flustered Lee Hyunsung blinked and stammered.
Jung Heewon clicked her tongue.
“Wow, you really were watching. Such a stalker······ But isn't 100 coins a bit stingy?”
I turned my gaze to the two children practicing [Taming]. They were continually giving orders to the enormous dragon. Perhaps she sensed my gaze, because Shin Yoosung smiled sweetly into empty space.
[A constellation who does not yet have a name smiles fondly.]

Ways of Survival often compared the relationship between a constellation and an incarnation to that of a parent and child. I'd never had a child, but watching Shin Yoosung, I felt as though I could understand what it was like.
A bond forged from something stronger than blood, perhaps. The feeling that someone was so very small and fragile, yet so precious that you didn't know what to do······.
Of course, just as not every father in the world was a good father, not every constellation would feel as I did. Incarnations being betrayed by their sponsors was a common occurrence.
Kraaaaar—!
The grade-2 evolved species, the ‘Chimera Dragon,’ let out a fierce roar.

It still didn't seem to obey very well, but with that creature joining the party, our fighting strength had truly skyrocketed. It was a grade-2 species now, but if it eventually surpassed grade 1 and became a transcendent species, that dragon would become a monster even constellations feared.
Watching the Chimera Dragon, Lee Jihye sighed as though she were envious.
“Damn it, I should've picked a better sponsor too. I thought I'd hit the jackpot when Grandpa Duke of Loyalty and Warfare showed up······.”
Honestly, the one who barely put in any effort complained the most.
She didn't even know how good a sponsor the Duke of Loyalty and Warfare was······ I'd have to set aside a day to teach her a proper lesson.
After taking a general look at everyone, I gave a light sigh and gathered my thoughts.
‘This should be enough to clear the next scenario.’

Lee Jihye and Gong Pildu's growth was a little disappointing, but the situation wasn't bad. We even had Yoo Sangah, a character outside the original cast. Once we escaped the [Seoul Dome], progressing through the subsequent scenarios should be fairly easy.
“Master! Aren't there any skills that let you get stronger without a sponsor? Teach me some!”
“They're beyond you as you are now.”

Yoo Joonghyuk also seemed to have overcome his Regression Depression to some extent. If we kept following the <Yoo Joonghyuk Route> like this, I wouldn't need to worry too much about the characters' survival anymore.
The problem lay with me instead.
[A great Fate desires your death.]
I looked at the ‘Fate message’ that still hadn't disappeared.
After experiencing a death caused by my mother this time, I'd entertained a little hope that my Fate might have been fulfilled. But as expected, it hadn't.
Perhaps ‘who kills me’ wasn't the important issue.
What mattered was that I couldn't evade this Fate through a ‘resurrection loophole.’
‘Those fucking nebulas······.’

Ultimately, things had come to this because I had changed too many scenarios. The excessive attention I'd drawn by ascending to constellation status had also played a large part. At this rate, even if I somehow prolonged my life through resurrection, the problems would never stop.
‘Something like this can't happen again.’
The recent [Eater of Dreams] incident alone was proof enough.
An Outer God's descent had nearly wiped out all my companions.
It didn't matter for me, since I could resurrect, but the same wasn't true of the others.
None of my companions could come back to life after dying. And if Yoo Joonghyuk died, everything would come to nothing.
None of it would have happened in the first place if I hadn't been there.
[The nebula <Vedas> is awaiting your resurrection.]
[The nebula <Papyrus> is awaiting your resurrection.]
[The nebula <Olympus> is awaiting your resurrection.]
Watching the nebulas hold their breath and wait for an opportunity, I thought and thought.
I had already drawn their attention, and I was still far too weak to oppose them.
How could I protect my companions and shake those bastards off······?
‘Is that really the only way?’
That was when a system message appeared.
[All resurrection conditions have been fulfilled!]
[The benefit of the attribute ‘Eight Lives’ activates!]
Before I knew it, it was time to return.
[Your body is resurrected from death.]
With a long shhhh, breath fills my lungs.

I say this every time, but the hardest thing to get used to is that first breath after resurrection. When I opened my eyes, pitch-black darkness surrounded me. Probably because my companions had put me in a coffin.
Damn it, I didn't understand why they insisted on putting someone who was going to come back to life in a coffin. Were they mocking me?
[The benefit of the attribute ‘Eight Lives’ is active.]
[The snake's third head is sacrificed.]
[This head's ability is ‘Fighting Spirit (鬪志).’]
Once again, I received the benefit without fail.
The benefits granted through ‘Eight Lives’ had relatively minor effects compared with other high-level blessings, but they were still better than nothing.
The legs I had lost while dying had been restored to their original state. All that remained was to kick the coffin lid open and get out.
“Ohhh! The rumors were true!”
“He really came back to life!”

The moment I pushed hard against the lid with a creak, the people gathered around me erupted in cheers. Word of my resurrection must have spread, because incarnations of all kinds had gathered to watch me.
[Your repeated resurrections increase your fame among incarnations.]
[Your Status rises slightly.]
Baaaang!
Jung Heewon, who happened to be nearby, welcomed me by firing [Hell Flames Ignition] into the air like celebratory fireworks.
Using that skill like that would send the constellations of <Eden> into a rage.
“Congratulations on your resurrection.”
“······Please don't put me in a coffin next time.”
“Wait just a moment. I'll go get the others.”
No sooner had Jung Heewon left than indirect messages from the constellations poured into my ears.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ rejoices at your resurrection.]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ congratulates you on your return.]
[The constellation ‘Goryeo’s First Sword’ praises your courage.]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ rummages through their pockets, grumbling.]
[Many constellations are greatly amazed by your achievement.]
[You have received 90,000 coins in sponsorship.]
It seemed they were all troubled by their failure to help me the day before yesterday.
I was a little hurt, but I could understand. If they had helped me even at the cost of confronting other nebulas, that would have been more suspicious.
[The evaluation of your achievement is complete.]
[You have acquired a ‘Quasi-myth-grade’ Story.]
[You have acquired the Story ‘One Who Killed an Outer God’!]
[The achievement of this Story causes several Outer Gods to harbor hostility toward you.]
[The achievement of this Story causes some Outer Gods to become curious about you.]
[The achievement of this Story causes several ‘Great Old Ones’ to watch you.]
[Your modifier will be announced soon.]
A Quasi-myth-grade Story, of all things······.
I was a little disappointed that I hadn't received a Myth-grade Story, but this was still enough to be reasonably satisfied with.

If I'd fought a ‘Great Old One,’ I would certainly have received a Myth-grade Story. But if I'd faced a being of that magnitude, I would have been annihilated before I could even attempt a conversation.
[You have achieved a new Story during the assessment.]
[Your Status is reevaluated following the acquisition of a Story that surpasses your existing Stories.]
[Your Status will be announced in the next scenario.]
[Your fifth Story is still in progress.]
I'd thought I would be lucky to start at the bottom of Historical-grade, but at this rate, my announced Status might place me fairly high within Historical-grade.
So it would be announced in the next scenario.
The timing seemed quite good.
The long-awaited tenth main scenario, <The 73rd Demon King>.
This was the final scenario to be held in the [Seoul Dome], and participation was extremely limited.
Only the people ranked first and second in the Dark Castle could challenge the scenario.
Of course, they wouldn't be challenging it alone. Each could form a team with up to four other rankers.
[Your current Dark Castle ranking is 2nd.]
I could bring a total of four companions myself.
But that number alone would make it difficult to face the enemy on the next floor.
In other words, completing this scenario required the help of the Dark Castle's number-one ranker.
The question was who that number-one ranker was.
“Kim Dokja.”
No sooner had I thought it than a voice came from behind me.
A chuckle escapes me.
······Well, who else would be number one?
“Yoo Joonghyuk, you're ranked first right now, aren't you?”
“Are you referring to the Dark Castle rankings?”
When I nodded, Yoo Joonghyuk immediately answered.
“I am first. Things are different from the Seoul rankings.”
Apparently, this bastard really was still bothered about not taking first place back then.
What a petty fucker.
Grumbling inwardly, I spoke.
“I need your help. As you know, there's a limit on how many people we can bring to the next scenario. Unless you and I divide them between us······.”
I could see my companions running toward us in the distance.

Lee Hyunsung and Lee Gilyoung jostling each other to get to the front was a particularly remarkable sight. It wasn't as though I was giving out a prize for coming first. I didn't understand why they were doing it.
Even as I talked at length, Yoo Joonghyuk gave no reply.
Something felt strange, so I looked up. Yoo Joonghyuk was looking down at me with a serious gaze.
“Kim Dokja, what is your objective?”
“Objective? What objective?”
“Is reaching ‘the end of all scenarios’ your ultimate goal?”
I hesitated briefly before answering.
“Well, more or less.”
“Can you promise that, no matter what happens, you will not give up on that goal?”
······What was with this bastard all of a sudden?
I wanted to laugh it off, but seeing Yoo Joonghyuk ask without any change in his expression, I couldn't help becoming serious too.
“Of course I won't give up. But why?”
“It's nothing.”
Yoo Joonghyuk withdrew his gaze from me and looked toward the others. His left eyebrow was twitching. Watching that eyebrow wriggle like a caterpillar left an uneasy chill in one corner of my heart.
Having read Ways of Survival to the end, I know.
Yoo Joonghyuk's left eyebrow only twitches when he has made a grave decision.
And after he makes a grave decision, there is always a high likelihood of death followed by regression.
Wondering what nonsense this bastard was plotting now, I was just about to use [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint] when the others arrived. Before I could even open my mouth, Yoo Joonghyuk beat me to it.
“I will announce the participants in the tenth scenario.”
The backlash against Yoo Joonghyuk's unilateral announcement was enormous.
“How can he just decide that all by himself?”
Once Yoo Joonghyuk had finished his arbitrary announcement and disappeared, Jung Heewon was the first to shout.
“‘We leave in three days! Raise your rankings by then yourselves!’ He says that and walks off, and we're supposed to scramble around on our own?”
“Why didn't you say that while that bastard was here?”
“······Would you have, Dokja-ssi?”
“No.”
Jung Heewon was still fuming, apparently unable to get over her anger.
“Still, doing what Yoo Joonghyuk says will probably give us a better chance of survival.”
“Whose side are you on, Dokja-ssi?”
I glanced at Yoo Joonghyuk, who was glaring our way from a distance, then shrugged and smiled.
“First of all, it's good to see everyone. This makes my third resurrection.”

Only then did the companions who had been frozen by Yoo Joonghyuk's overbearing presence begin to smile awkwardly, one by one. Lee Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung each clung tightly to one of my legs, while Lee Hyunsung nodded with a slightly melancholy expression.
“Congratulations on your resurrection. It's happened several times already, but I still can't get used to it.”
“I think I'd be sad if you did get used to it. For now, let's sort things out.”
Yoo Joonghyuk's unilateral announcement had been as follows.
—We will divide into two teams. My team and Kim Dokja's team. Each will be allotted four people.
—The four joining my team will be Lee Hyunsung, Gong Pildu, Lee Jihye, and Lee Seolhwa.
—Kim Dokja's team will consist of these four: Jung Heewon, Shin Yoosung, Lee Gilyoung, and Yoo Sangah.

In the end, the roster was more or less the same as the core group that had taken part in our battles so far. He meant for the companions who had been fighting together all along to take on the tenth scenario too. Perhaps he was being considerate of me, or perhaps it was convenient for him. Given Yoo Joonghyuk's personality, the latter was probably far more likely.
No one seemed particularly dissatisfied with the roster itself. The only person looking downcast was Lee Hyunsung.
“I'd like to be on your team, Dokja-ssi······.”
“We're all going together anyway, so it probably won't matter much which team you're on.”
I patted Lee Hyunsung's shoulder and turned toward the others.
The first person whose eyes met mine was Yoo Sangah.
Perhaps it had been too long, because even meeting her eyes somehow felt strange. After a moment, Jung Heewon poked me in the side.
“What is it? Can't get the garter belt and qipao out of your head?”
“······Are we still talking about that?”
“It was that shocking. We even gave it a name among ourselves: ‘The Kim Dokja Garter Belt Incident.’ But I'd rather die than wear one.”
“I wasn't hoping you would.”
At that, Lee Jihye shot her hand up.
“I'd be willing to wear one if it performed well! SSS-grade!”
“Stop teasing me.”
“I could wear something like that too, as long as its performance was good.”
“Why you too, Hyunsung-ssi······?”
“A soldier isn't picky about equipment.”
I was about to advise him not to exercise his soldierly spirit in such an odd direction when Uriel's message sounded from empty space.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ says that the constellation who made the garter belt was also a man.]
That had to be a joke, right? Damn it.
And a ‘constellation,’ at that?
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ smiles and says she will invite him over sometime.]
Come to think of it, this whole situation was Persephone's fault. If I ever went to the Underworld again, I'd definitely have to take it up with her.
“Let's leave that subject there······ What are everyone's rankings? You all know you have to be in the top ten to be on this roster, right?”
My companions answered in turn.
Jung Heewon went first.
“I'm fourth. Grandma Lee Boksoon passed her ranking on to me.”
“I'm eighth and Shin Yoosung is ninth, hyung. Oh, and I'm higher than Shin Yoosung!”
“I'm fifth. And Gong Pildu-ssi has stepped away for a while to raise his ranking. Han Sooyoung-ssi too.”
Right, there was Han Sooyoung.
As though she had read my thoughts, Yoo Sangah asked.
“Han Sooyoung-ssi wasn't on that roster. Are you leaving her behind?”
“No, we need to bring her. Han Sooyoung is quite helpful.”
Yoo Sangah smiled weakly at the mention of Han Sooyoung.
The others still didn't know that she had been the ‘First Apostle.’
Whenever Han Sooyoung came up, Yoo Sangah would feel as though she was lying, so she couldn't help feeling bad. I'd have to tell them about it sometime, but I wasn't sure I'd get the chance.
Jung Heewon, who had been listening beside us, spoke.
“Only ten people can go up in total. How are you going to bring Han Sooyoung-ssi?”

“In principle, only ten can go, but there's a hidden piece. One of the items you can obtain in the [Dark Castle] is called a [Six Man Card]. If you use it, someone who isn't on a team can participate in the next scenario too.”

“······Honestly, those damned hidden pieces. Is there anything else you could tell us? We ought to know what's coming in the next scenario that warrants all this fuss. You're always whispering with Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi, just the two of you.”
“Whispering? I'm not very comfortable with that wording.”
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ snorts through her nose.]
Jung Heewon looked at me with a bright smile.
“Then tell us. Show us you're different from Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi, Kim Dokja-ssi.”
When I looked around, everyone was gazing at me with shining eyes, like grandchildren waiting for their grandmother to tell them a folktale.
If I were a storyteller, I might have opened with something fitting like ‘Once upon a time, there lived a hero.’ But I'm Kim Dokja, a reader, not Kim Jakga, a writer.
“Have any of you heard of beings called ‘Demon Kings’?”
Demon King (魔王).
At the unexpected term, my companions looked at one another.
“Well······ A king of demons? Something like that?”
“I know! They're in anime all the time!”
I nodded at Lee Gilyoung's shout.
“More or less.”
It was a little different according to the lore of Ways of Survival, but this wasn't the place to ramble through an explanation.
“The tenth scenario is a scenario where we fight that ‘Demon King.’”
Lee Hyunsung nodded with a low hum.
“Dokkaebis, returnees, tentacle monsters······ I did think it was about time something like a Demon King appeared.”
Lee Jihye, who had been listening, asked.
“But isn't a Demon King ridiculously strong? That demon marquis was already that powerful······ Just how strong is it compared to that?”
I considered for a moment before answering.
“Constellation-level.”
There was a phrase used to describe Demon Kings in Ways of Survival.
Constellations (星座) who had not ascended.
Quite literally, Demon Kings were ‘constellations’ who had remained rooted in the mortal world.
Her face turning pale, Lee Jihye pressed me.
“How are we supposed to beat something like that? Oh, are you and Master going to beat it yourselves again, ajusshi?”
“No, this time we'll all beat it together.”
“······Can't I just not go up?”
“We can only beat it if we all fight together. It was pure luck that Yoo Joonghyuk and I defeated that god. We won't get a lucky break like that twice.”
“Don't worry. It's true that Demon Kings are as strong as ‘constellations,’ but the one upstairs isn't quite at that level.”
“Then?”
I hesitated briefly.
I wasn't sure I could spill that much information all at once right now.
Because this information concerned not only Demon Kings, but also the constellations of the <Star Stream>.
After thinking for a moment, I was just about to explain through [Group Chat] when—
[I'll explain that.]
Perhaps aware of my predicament, a voice came from empty space.
[It's been a while, everyone. Ah, you have no idea how frustrating it's been, not being able to speak······ Haha, are your scenario preparations going well?]
It was Bihyung.
Originally, only 72 beings were recognized as ‘Demon Kings’ in the <Star Stream>.
Like constellations, they had modifiers, and each controlled a different domain in the Demon Realm.
Though they couldn't compare to a ‘nebula,’ they were still beings who led a ‘faction.’
They mocked the constellations' obsession with their honor as constellations and remained on land that even the dokkaebis had abandoned.
Perhaps that was why. The constellations had come to hate Demon Kings as much as ‘Outer Gods,’ and this [Dark Castle] scenario had been created with that inclination in mind.
Watch incarnations fight, and kill a Demon King too.
You could say it was a scenario made to give the constellations a satisfying payoff.
“Oh, please! I told you I'm not going!”
Drag, drag, drag, drag.
Over those three days, I tracked down Han Sooyoung, who had been hiding on the outskirts of the [Dark Castle].

She had hidden herself so thoroughly that I might never have found her without the [Binding Rope] and [Person Search] I'd purchased from the Dokkaebi Bag. Han Sooyoung shouted as she struggled desperately.
“I'm not fighting anymore! I'm just going to sit around here, then leave once you clear the scenario!”
“You have to come too.”
“I don't want to fight a Demon King!”
“The 73rd Demon King was thrown together for this. You know that too, don't you?”

As I'd said earlier, only 72 beings in the <Star Stream> had been recognized as having the Status of a ‘Demon King.’ Yet this scenario was titled [The 73rd Demon King]. In other words, the one upstairs wasn't an ‘official Demon King.’
“It's still a ‘Demon King,’ so it'll be one of the strongest beings we've encountered so far. But it isn't as strong as a Narrative-grade constellation. We have a fighting chance.”
“The difficulty might have changed. How many times has it changed while I've been with you?”
“Dokkaebis can't arbitrarily change a main scenario's difficulty. That's under the <Star Stream>'s jurisdiction.”
“You think dokkaebis are the only danger? Have you already forgotten what happened three days ago?”
It wasn't strange that Han Sooyoung was so thoroughly fed up.
Knowing the original story's course would only make it worse.
“If we keep going through the scenarios like this, all your companions will be wiped out before long. You know the <nebulas> are all after you right now, don't you?”
“······I know. That's why I'm preparing carefully too.”
“Preparing? Seriously, is this something preparation can fix? How do you know what'll happen even in the very next scenario?”
We had just reached the campsite, so I silently pointed toward the others.
My companions were training in their respective formations. Facing an imagined enemy, they shifted formation and practiced combining their skills.
“Gilyoung and Yoosung, to the rear! Yoo Sangah-ssi moves forward, and I'll take the position behind her!”
“Got it!”

Their calm, coordinated attacks were on an entirely different level from anything they'd done before. They used elemental properties to stack damage, and took advantage of the enemy's attack radius to rain down fire from a distance. Watching them closely, Han Sooyoung's mouth fell open.
“Wait, is that······ Did you analyze the Demon King's attack patterns?”
I nodded.
“Yes.”
“How much?”
“Almost all of them.”
It wasn't impossible.

I had the text file of Ways of Survival, and a considerable database of Yoo Joonghyuk's battles with the 73rd Demon King had accumulated. Moreover, Yoo Joonghyuk had fought the 73rd Demon King in his second round too. With practical experience and thorough theoretical knowledge combined, developing a complete strategy for the next scenario wasn't entirely impossible.
Han Sooyoung looked genuinely overwhelmed.
“······You really are a crazy bastard.”
“Do you still think the next scenario will be difficult?”
The 73rd Demon King was strong, but if we went up with preparations this thorough, there would be no problem.
It might even turn out to be the easiest scenario we'd attempted so far.
Before long, the companions who had been training gathered around us one by one.
“Has everyone finished raising their rankings?”
Jung Heewon answered on everyone's behalf.
“We're all in the top ten. Jihye and Pildu-ssi were actually cutting it close, but they moved up automatically this morning.”
“Automatically?”
That kind of advancement occurred in only one circumstance.
When a higher-ranked person died.
Han Sooyoung already looked apprehensive.
“A top-ten ranker suddenly died? Something's strange······ Hey, I really think I'd be better off not going······.
“You're here, Kim Dokja. Are you bringing that woman too?”
At Yoo Joonghyuk's sudden appearance, Han Sooyoung swiftly hid behind me.
Apparently she was still afraid of Yoo Joonghyuk.
When I nodded, Yoo Joonghyuk, who had been glaring disapprovingly at Han Sooyoung, took a [Six Man Card] out of his clothes.
[Incarnation ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ has used a Six Man Card.]
[Incarnation ‘Han Sooyoung’ is recruited as a special participant in the scenario.]
[Incarnation ‘Han Sooyoung’ has joined the team of incarnation ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’.]
Han Sooyoung was horrified by the messages that appeared.
“Wh-what is this! Hey! Why am I on his team!”
“All right, we're about to leave, so everyone get ready.”
At my words, everyone gathered by team.
Yoo Joonghyuk's team assembled first.
In order: Lee Seolhwa, Lee Jihye, Lee Hyunsung, and Gong Pildu. Plus Han Sooyoung, still complaining.
The sight of elements from the original story strangely mingled with things outside it stirred an odd feeling in me.
A luxury only the reader of Ways of Survival could enjoy, perhaps.
My team then lined up in turn.
Jung Heewon, Yoo Sangah, Shin Yoosung. And Lee Gilyoung too.
Compared with Yoo Joonghyuk's disciplined team, ours had a relaxed atmosphere.
I looked at each of my companions with care.
“······What's with that sappy look?”
“Nothing. It just feels different, looking back······.”
Despite Jung Heewon's reproach, I quietly smiled.
Looking at these people who had followed me faithfully all this way, my heart somehow swelled, yet for some reason it ached too.
That feeling seemed especially strong since I'd spoken with the [Fourth Wall].
Perhaps that was why I had prepared even more thoroughly for this scenario.
I was now afraid of losing them.
“Oh, you know our team has a sixth member too, right?”
At my words, my teammates turned their heads, following my gaze.
A figure stood hesitantly a few steps away.
“Don't stay over there. Come here.”
We had obtained a total of two [Six Man Cards].
Just as Han Sooyoung had joined Yoo Joonghyuk's team, our team had a sixth man too.
A sixth woman, to be precise.
“······Sookyung-ssi wanted to go with you too.”
“Right now, it will be more helpful to have you with us.”
Jeon Woochi's incarnation, Cho Youngran, looked at me with mixed emotions in her eyes.
I had asked my mother to let me include her in this expedition as a special addition.
Because quite a few of Jeon Woochi's stigmas could prove useful in an emergency.
“Have you talked with Sookyung-ssi?”
“A little.”
Perhaps because of the aftereffects of emerging from the [Fourth Wall], my mother was in no condition to participate in the next scenario.
Through the [Fourth Wall], I had learned many things about my mother.
Not only about the past she'd hidden, but also about what she'd experienced after joining the scenarios.
Unlike me, who knew every story in the original novel, my mother had endured one desperate struggle after another.

She had repeatedly paid exorbitant prices to obtain help from constellations, deliberately let the reincarnator Nirvana capture her to steal their memories, and even entered a contract with a <nebula> to protect me.
Yet even after learning all of that, I couldn't find anything to say to my mother.
I decided to think that perhaps the time simply hadn't come yet.
Someday, once the scenarios had ended safely, the day would come when we, mother and son, could share a real ‘story.’
Perhaps my mother knew that too, because she didn't say much this time. She merely looked at me for a long time, then turned her eyes away and said this.
—I trust your choice.
I didn't know why, but hearing those words gave me a strange feeling.
Perhaps, just as I had read my mother through the [Fourth Wall], she too had read something in me.
“Let's go.”
We began to move.
Our destination was the altar at the center of the <Abyss Plains>.
As on the first floor of the Dark Castle, we could use an altar here to move to the next floor.
Perhaps bored by the walk, Jung Heewon spoke.
“It bothers me that the nebulas are so quiet.”
